questions.q: What is a tree, in the chart of accounts context?
options: A hierarchical structure built from a value set's values, organizing them into parent-child relationships for rollup purposes
A type of cross-validation rule
A ledger's calendar structure
A list of enabled currencies
questions.explain: A tree organizes value set values into parent-child hierarchies, enabling rollup reporting.

questions.q: In a tree, which values do transactions actually post to?
options: Parent (summary) values only
Detail (child) values with posting allowed, not the summary parent nodes
Every value in the tree equally
Only values from a different value set entirely
questions.explain: Transactions post to detail/child values; parent (summary) nodes exist for rollup reporting rather than direct posting.

questions.q: Why does a tree support multiple tree versions?
options: Tree versions have no real purpose in Oracle Fusion
Because trees are deleted and recreated every fiscal year
Because organizational hierarchies change over time, and tree versions capture when a given hierarchy shape was true
Because each legal entity requires a separate tree version
questions.explain: Tree versions, each with their own effective date range, let a company capture historical and current hierarchy shapes without losing history.

questions.q: What benefit does running a report against a specific tree version provide?
options: It permanently changes the underlying value set
It disables posting for all detail values
It merges all legal entities into one ledger
It allows viewing numbers through the hierarchy shape that was actually true for that period, such as last year's structure for last year's numbers
questions.explain: Reports and allocations can target a specific tree version, letting a company view historical data through the hierarchy that was actually in effect at the time.

questions.q: Besides reporting, where else does this lesson say hierarchies reduce maintenance?
options: Legal entity registration and business unit assignment
Cross-validation rules and allocation rules, which can reference a parent node instead of listing every individual value
Currency enablement and daily rate imports
Accounting calendar period naming
questions.explain: Cross-validation rules (Lesson 24) and allocation rules can reference a hierarchy node, automatically covering new children added underneath it later.
